newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal considers buying U.S. F-16 jets.
newsitem.headline: Portugal considers buying U.S. F-16 jets.

text.p: Portugal is considering buying F-16 military jets from the United States, John Shalikashvili, chairman of the U.S. joint chiefs of staff, said on Friday.

"We have been asked by the government of Portugal to provide price and availability data on F-16s. We have done that gladly," Shalikashvili told a news conference, winding up a three-day visit to Lisbon to discuss bilateral and other military issues.

"We are awaiting deliberations within the government of Portugal to let us know whether the government is interested in purchasing those F-16s," he added. "But we are prepared to sell them if the government of Portugal is interested."
Shalikashvili and his Portuguese host, Admiral Fuzeta da Ponte, declined to say how many planes Portugal might buy or what they might cost.

According to a government document made available to Reuters, the U.S. Defence Department told Congress this month that the Portuguese government had requested the purchase of 25 used F-16A/Bs and spare parts for a total estimated cost of $258 million.
The F-16, a mid-1980s multi-role fighter, was originally built by General Dynamics and later by Lockheed Martin.
"The sale will enable Portugal to augment its current F-16 aircraft inventory and to develop and maintain a continuous air defence capability within its national boundaries," the document said.

"This sale will contribute to the foreign policy and national security objectives of the U.S. by improving the military capabilities of Portugal while enhancing weapon system standardisation and inter-operability with the U.S. forces in the region," it added.
